beats.spoken: What does the little hourglass on some cosmetic packs mean?

It belongs to the date of minimum durability. Under Article 19 of the EU cosmetics regulation, that's the date until which a product, stored properly, keeps doing its original job and stays safe. The rule covers both the container and the packaging.
Before the date comes either the hourglass from Annex VII, or the words “best used before the end of”. Storage conditions are added where needed.

The date is month and year, or day, month and year, in that order. It's only required if a product lasts 30 months or less. If it lasts longer, the open-jar symbol takes its place. Symbol or words: either is allowed.

beats.spoken: The US is different. Cosmetics there don't need expiration dates. Drugs do, and in the US sunscreens are drugs. Make-up with an SPF even counts as both. There, drugs have to stay safe and effective until their expiration date.
For you, that means: look for the hourglass or the words, read the month and year, and check for any storage instructions.
Read the date first, then apply. Beauty knowledge, clearly explained: follow Dewlane.
